purpose: Curated, mutually distinct design choices. `helen design direction` combines them with a seed so two projects do not converge on the same look. Tags express affinity; the generator keeps each direction coherent and different from the others.
bannedDefaults: Purple, indigo or violet-to-pink gradients on backgrounds or headlines
Inter, Roboto, Arial or the system font as the only typeface
Three equal feature cards, each with an icon, a heading and two lines
A centered hero with a blurred gradient blob behind it
Glassmorphism (blur plus translucent white) as the default surface
The same large corner radius and soft shadow on every surface
Stock imagery of handshakes, laptops on desks or abstract globes
Words like elevate, unlock, seamless, supercharge, revolutionize, next-generation, all-in-one, welcome to
Invented testimonials, logos or counts of customers
Neon glow on dark as the only personality
The sticky nav, hero, logo cloud, feature triad, pricing triad sequence copied unchanged

concept.name: Editorial broadsheet
concept.summary: A reading experience first: columns, rules, bylines, datelines, a clear front page.
signature: A drop cap and a running folio on every page
Pull quotes set in the display face between columns
A colophon footer that credits typefaces and people
risks: Dense text needs a strict measure and spacing scale
Needs real headlines, not marketing slogans

concept.name: Swiss grid
concept.summary: International typographic style: a strict grid, flush-left ragged-right text, scale contrast, almost no decoration.
signature: Oversized section numerals anchored to the grid
One accent color used only for the single action per view
Asymmetric blocks that always snap to the same columns
risks: Can read cold without warm copy
Alignment bugs are very visible

concept.name: Technical blueprint
concept.summary: Drawing sheets: hairlines, dimensions, labeled parts, coordinates, a title block.
signature: Callout lines that label real parts of the product
A title block footer with revision and date
Section marks like A-A and detail views
risks: Annotations must be true or the metaphor becomes decoration
Thin lines need care for contrast

concept.name: Craft studio
concept.summary: Made by hand: paper, ink, small irregularities, process shown honestly.
signature: Photographs of the actual workbench with handwritten captions
A batch or maker's mark on each product
Process steps shown as a contact sheet
risks: Fake roughness looks worse than none
Needs real photography

concept.name: Museum catalogue
concept.summary: Plates with captions, catalogue numbers, generous space, one object at a time.
signature: Catalogue numbers and dimensions as captions
One object per viewport with wall-text beside it
An index of plates at the end
risks: Very sparse pages need excellent images
Easy to hide the call to action

concept.name: Field notebook
concept.summary: Notes from the field: marginalia, sketches, timestamps, observations in order.
signature: Margin notes that react to the main text
Dated entries instead of sections
Sketched diagrams over photographs
risks: Handwriting fonts overused turn into costume
Chronology must match what the user needs

concept.name: Brutalist poster
concept.summary: Raw and loud: huge type, hard edges, few colors, nothing hidden.
signature: One headline that fills the first viewport
Visible borders and unstyled form controls kept deliberately
Link underlines as the only decoration
risks: Accessibility and readability must not suffer for attitude
Wrong for conservative audiences

concept.name: Retro terminal
concept.summary: Monospaced text, command-line motifs, status lines, a calm phosphor palette.
signature: A status line with real information
Navigation as commands that actually work
Output-style tables for pricing or specs
risks: A cliche unless content is genuinely technical
Long monospaced text tires readers

concept.name: Transit signage
concept.summary: Wayfinding: bold color blocks, arrows, pictograms, a line map of the product.
signature: A line-map of the user journey as navigation
Pictograms drawn to one grid
Destination boards for key facts
risks: Needs a consistent pictogram set
Color coding must not be the only signal

concept.name: Packaging label
concept.summary: The page is the label: ingredients, batch numbers, stamps, honest small print.
signature: An ingredients or materials list as a feature
Stamps and seals that carry real facts
Batch or edition numbers
risks: Small print must stay legible
Works best for physical goods

concept.name: Cinematic storyboard
concept.summary: Scenes and frames: letterboxed images, subtitles as copy, scroll as editing.
signature: Subtitle-style captions for the key sentences
Frame numbers and a progress line
Hard cuts between scenes instead of fades
risks: Heavy media needs a performance budget
Scroll hijacking harms usability

concept.name: Letterpress stationery
concept.summary: Cream stock, deep impressions, hairlines, small caps, correspondence.
signature: Small caps and ligatures in headings
Hairline rules and a monogram
Copy written as a letter, signed
risks: Low contrast hairlines on cream
Can feel precious for utilitarian products

concept.name: Data atlas
concept.summary: Maps and charts are the interface: annotated visualizations carry the story.
signature: A hero visualization of the product's own data
Annotations written like map legends
Small multiples instead of paragraphs
risks: Charts must be accessible with text alternatives
Needs real data

concept.name: Sticker sheet
concept.summary: A collage of bold shapes and labels, slightly rotated, playful but organized.
signature: Die-cut shaped badges for features
A peel-off interaction on one element
Hand-placed overlaps on a clear underlying grid
risks: Rotation and overlap break on small screens
Can look childish for serious products

type.name: Soft serif with a clean sans
type.notes: Fraunces has optical-size and softness axes; use high softness only for large display.

type.name: Quiet serif display with a neutral sans
type.notes: Instrument Serif has one weight; build hierarchy with size and spacing.

type.name: Newspaper serif with a news grotesque
type.notes: Use Newsreader for headlines and long reading, the grotesque for interface and captions.

type.name: Quirky grotesque with a reading serif
type.notes: Bricolage has strong personality at display sizes; keep body text in Literata.

type.name: Wide and condensed grotesque with a book serif
type.notes: Archivo's width axis allows poster-scale condensed headlines.

type.name: Mono and sans from one family
type.notes: One family keeps rhythm consistent; use mono for labels, numerals and headings.

type.name: Quirky mono with a friendly sans
type.notes: Space Mono is strongly characterful; avoid it for long text.

type.name: Mono labels with a serif voice
type.notes: Serif for statements, mono for data and captions: a deliberate contrast.

type.name: High-contrast display serif with a plain sans
type.notes: Gloock is for large sizes only; thin strokes vanish small.

type.name: Sturdy friendly serif with a geometric sans
type.notes: A single-weight display serif that stays approachable.

type.name: Wide expressive display with a neutral sans
type.notes: Syne ExtraBold is very wide; test headlines at 375 px.

type.name: Rounded wide display with a technical sans
type.notes: Unbounded works for short headlines and numerals only.

type.name: Old-style serif with a modern grotesque
type.notes: Caslon gives gravitas; pair with a restrained sans for interface.

type.name: Screen serif with a humanist grotesque
type.notes: Spectral is designed for screen reading; use light weights for display.

type.name: Bookish serif with a code mono
type.notes: Good for notebook-like pages mixing prose and code.

type.name: Poster condensed with a book serif
type.notes: Anton for one huge headline per view, never for body.

color.name: Cobalt and ink on warm white

layout.name: Asymmetric twelve columns
layout.summary: Headline across eight columns, body offset into the remaining space; whitespace carries the hierarchy.

layout.name: Baseline modular grid
layout.summary: Everything snaps to one baseline and module size, like a catalogue page.

layout.name: Single column long form
layout.summary: One reading column of about 60 characters with side notes in the margin.

layout.name: Fixed split screen
layout.summary: A fixed panel carries the title and actions while the other side scrolls.

layout.name: Sticky numbered index
layout.summary: A sticky table of contents with numbered sections beside the content.

layout.name: Rules and lists, no cards
layout.summary: Sections separated by hairline rules; content as lists and tables instead of boxes.

layout.name: Full-bleed scenes
layout.summary: Each viewport is a scene of image or type with one idea.

layout.name: Overlapping collage on a hidden grid
layout.summary: Panels overlap and rotate slightly while a simple grid keeps order.

layout.name: Formal center axis
layout.summary: Symmetrical, ceremonial layout with a central axis and generous margins.

layout.name: Information-dense panels
layout.summary: Tables, small type and tight spacing for expert users who scan.

motion.name: Almost still
motion.summary: No decorative motion; focus and hover transitions of 120 ms or less.
motion.guard: Nothing to disable for reduced motion.

motion.name: Snappy and mechanical
motion.summary: 120-180 ms ease-out transitions, no bounce, state changes that feel like switches.

motion.name: Soft and inertial
motion.summary: Gentle 400-700 ms reveals on scroll, restrained parallax on one element.
motion.guard: Disable parallax and reveals under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: Typographic reveals
motion.summary: Headlines reveal line by line through a mask; nothing else moves.
motion.guard: Show the text immediately when motion is reduced.

motion.name: Scroll narrative
motion.summary: One pinned, scroll-driven sequence tells the central story.
motion.guard: Needs a performance budget, no scroll hijacking, and a static fallback.

motion.name: Cursor reactive
motion.summary: A single key object responds subtly to the pointer.
motion.guard: Pointer-only enhancement; keyboard and touch get a static state.

motion.name: Page-to-page view transitions
motion.summary: Cross-document view transitions carry shared elements between pages.
motion.guard: Feature-detect and fall back to instant navigation.

motion.name: Slow ambient loop
motion.summary: One CSS-only background animation that takes over a minute to repeat.
motion.guard: Pause it under prefers-reduced-motion and when the tab is hidden.

imagery.name: Real photography
imagery.summary: Natural light, the real product and people, shot consistently.
imagery.needs: A photographer or a shot list the team can actually deliver.

imagery.name: One illustrator's style
imagery.summary: One consistent illustrated world instead of stock icons.
imagery.needs: A commissioned or consistent set; never mix styles.

imagery.name: Typography as the image
imagery.summary: Large type, numerals and marks do the visual work.
imagery.needs: Strong type choices and tight copy.

imagery.name: Diagrams and data
imagery.summary: Diagrams, charts and maps explain the product.

imagery.name: Paper and print texture
imagery.summary: Risograph, grain and paper surfaces under flat shapes.
imagery.needs: Subtle, optimized textures; never over text.

imagery.name: One hero object
imagery.summary: A single product or 3D object, presented with care.
imagery.needs: A 3D budget and a still fallback.

imagery.name: Annotated interface
imagery.summary: Real screenshots with callouts that teach.
imagery.needs: Up-to-date screens that match the product.

imagery.name: Text only
imagery.summary: No pictures; hierarchy, rhythm and copy carry everything.

voice.name: Plainspoken
voice.summary: Short sentences, concrete nouns, no adjectives that cannot be checked.

voice.name: Dry wit
voice.summary: Understatement and the occasional deadpan aside, never at the reader's expense.

voice.name: Calm authority
voice.summary: Measured and precise; claims arrive with their evidence.

voice.name: Warm and personal
voice.summary: First person, specific people and places, a maker's voice.

voice.name: Technical and exact
voice.summary: Units, versions, limits and failure modes stated up front.

voice.name: Restrained and poetic
voice.summary: Few words, with rhythm; imagery used once, not everywhere.

voice.name: Direct and urgent
voice.summary: Imperatives, deadlines and numbers; says what to do now.

voice.name: Playful and conversational
voice.summary: Writes the way a friendly expert talks, with jokes that carry information.
